text:
Chapter Twenty-Nine


Like every other moment since he’d waltzed into her life, Arthur Taliesin was currently making Maggie’s life difficult. He sat across from her in the botany lab, looking so proud of himself for that comment, which he knew would leave her squirming and blushing. And, sure enough, her stomach had flipped, her breath had hitched, and heat had spread along her whole body as that one sentence set off a barrage of fantasies she didn’t even know she had.


Despite the distraction, Maggie carefully ripped the gloaming creeper into fine ribbons and added it to the first boiling mixture. As it began to leach into the water, it turned the liquid to a light mauve. Once they were done, after the decoction had had time to settle, it would turn a brilliant aubergine color. Ignoring Arthur’s comment, though his smug smirk still hadn’t fallen, she looked again at Dr. Silva’s procedure. “After the first extraction, it will need to be exposed to two hours’ worth of afternoon light. Then it needs time to settle before it will sit out beneath the waning crescent moon for three nights. Then another three weeks of settling.” She bit her lip. “We’re going to have a lot of downtime.”


“Mm-hmm,” Arthur murmured as he wrote down the temperature of the first phase of the decoction for their records. When he looked up from the notes, he had that cocksure grin on his face again. “I think we’ll be quite busy.”


“Oh?”


“Of course.” He leaned forward just slightly, and his voice was low like he was about to say something lascivious. Instead he said, “There are so many wards we should be fortifying.”


Maggie groaned. He was right, of course. Already the wards that had been strengthened by students before they left for the summer had begun to fade. The force of the pall’s magic was putting too much pressure on them.


“Yes, absolutely. Obviously, we should be fortifying the wards. We have plenty of time for that. But what if you also took me to the beach?”


The small dose of sunlight Maggie had experienced in the Wilds when they’d walked beyond the influence of the pall had awoken something in her. Maggie needed sun. She needed to bask, to lie out like a lizard until she felt warm from the inside out, and to melt the effects of the pall from the outside in. Atlantia, with its broad, busy beaches, was not covered by the pall’s relentless cloud. Atlantia, where Arthur lived.


Arthur’s eyes flitted to her chest, completely covered by her lab coat, and she wondered if he was imagining her in a swimsuit. She already knew which one she’d wear—black and constructed out of what looked like two wide ribbons that wrapped around her cleavage and her waist. It was very annoying to put on and even worse to take off and she wanted to see if Arthur was up to the challenge.


“I feel bad taking a break from all this”—she gestured around them—“but it might be…” She didn’t finish the thought. It might be our only chance to do something fun. She was too aware of their impending deadline. “The decoction will be ready three and a half weeks from now. What if we just see how much we get done this week? If we fortify every ward and I get through most of the translation, we could go next Saturday. That will still give us a few days afterward to finish any last-minute preparations.”


She knew she was explaining too much, but he was watching her with a careful expression, and she was afraid of what his answer might be. Maybe she had misunderstood him. Maybe he didn’t want to see her outside of her apartment and the Hawthorn campus. She couldn’t blame him; they were only going to be together for the summer, even if reminding herself of that made her throat start to feel tight. But then he was talking, and Maggie had to ask him to repeat himself because she wasn’t sure she heard him correctly.


“I’d love to take you to the beach that Saturday, but we might have to take a break to watch a five-year-old pick flowers in the outfield,” he said, back to busying himself with the alembic in front of him. “My nephew’s baseball game is that day.”


Maggie paused. Surely he didn’t want her to go to his nephew’s baseball game? “Well, that you definitely can’t miss. We’ll find another day.”


He finally looked up from fiddling with the equipment. Behind his safety glasses and his eyeglasses, his expression was one that Maggie couldn’t quite interpret. “No, you’re right. There isn’t really another day. Besides, it won’t take long. They’re five and six, they’re lucky if they make it through half an hour. Come to the game.” He sounded sure, but Maggie couldn’t help her doubt. He seemed to sense her hesitation because he added quickly, “Invite Dahlia. Simon will be so happy to have a crowd cheering for him. We’ll have hot dogs and get irrationally angry at the opposing five-year-olds when they manage to score.”


Maggie couldn’t help the curve of her smile, or the flush of pleasure she felt at Arthur’s relief when she said, “I’ll ask Dahlia. You’re right, it’ll be fun.”



—


When the liquid had siphoned into the beaker, Maggie returned it to the container above the burner and adjusted the temperature until it was a slow, rolling boil. “It’s ready,” she called over to Arthur, who was removing his safety glasses and lab coat. He walked to one of the many old levers in the lab and began to crank the glass panel open. Ancient copper gears on the ceiling creaked to life, and cool, foggy air filled the lab. “Dr. Silva said we don’t have to babysit it. She’ll have her lab assistant check to make sure it isn’t boiling over or getting too cool.”


They decided to get lunch and meet back in their office, with Maggie returning to Ilex Hall and Arthur heading down to a café right off campus called Dot’s. Eventually, he returned with a crinkling bag filled with metal canisters of soup.


“I’ve never been over to Dot’s,” Arthur said as he unpacked their lunch. “It’s cute. Dot served me herself!”


Maggie laughed at his enthusiasm. “You met a celebrity. She hasn’t been behind the counter much since her ninetieth birthday.”


“That explains her granddaughter’s scowl.” He arranged the food on Maggie’s desk so he could position his office chair across from her. She opened her container of tomato soup and unwrapped the grilled cheese. Maggie had been the one to call the order in as Arthur walked, and she found a napkin tucked into her wrapped sandwich with Dot’s shaky handwriting—What a hunk! Maggie choked on the spoonful of soup she’d just sipped and tucked the napkin into her pocket. Arthur would be insufferable if he saw it.


Arthur had ordered a beef noodle soup with thin, stretchy noodles and a fragrant broth flavored with ginger. It was one of Maggie’s favorites, and she reached over with her spoon and stole a piece of beef and some broth. She sighed. Everything Dot and her granddaughter made was delicious.


When they finished eating, somehow they both ended up on the couch. Arthur sat with his knees bent, and Maggie with her legs over his, leaning against the armrest. They had a little over an hour where their time was not accounted for. It wasn’t enough to replenish any of the wards around campus or solve the problem of the incantation translation or adjust any calculations. They had no more rare ingredients to hunt for or experts to consult. So, for once, they took a break.


Both of them had reached for novels on Maggie’s shelves. Arthur chose a fantasy novel he had already read, losing himself in the pages quickly. Maggie picked a romance she’d been saving for a quiet moment just like this. She tossed a crocheted blanket over their legs against the chill coming through the window, which she’d opened to air out the stuffy office, and let herself get lost in the meet-cute.


Arthur’s hand rested on her thigh, and she barely noticed as he absentmindedly traced languid circles over her skirt, the silky fabric pulling up her thigh until his finger was on her skin. She glared at him over her paperback, but Arthur kept turning his pages, and she didn’t tell him to stop. She tried to focus on the words in front of her, but his fingers were trailing bigger and bigger circles, moving dangerously higher. She snapped her book shut and stood up, the blanket falling to the floor.


“What is it?” Arthur asked innocently. Maggie locked their office door and Arthur leaned back, looking entirely too satisfied for Maggie’s liking. His legs were spread wide, his hand resting on his inner thigh. He nearly took up the entire couch, the entire office.


They didn’t say a word to each other. Arthur’s eyes roamed over every inch of Maggie, every curve, every glimpse of her skin. In two steps, she was back in front of him, leaning forward and resting one hand on the worn arm of the couch, which propped her above him. Her other hand came up and stroked Arthur’s tense jaw.


“You’re breaking the rules,” he said through clenched teeth, shifting his hips.


“You broke them first.” As she said it, he reached up and grasped the hand she was using to stroke his jaw. His grip on her arm was strong and firm, but it didn’t hurt, and she liked it. With his other hand, he grabbed a fistful of her shirt and pulled her closer toward him. Her knees knocked against the edge of the couch between his spread legs. She gasped as his fingers snaked up the back of her neck and into her hair. “Whatever we start here we can’t finish here,” she said in a breathy voice. His hand moved from the front of her shirt to the crook of her hip, settling her between his legs. “We have to check on the decoction in half an hour.”


Maggie didn’t understand how she could still be wound so tight after the weekend they had, but he had already spun her into a frenzy with just his words. And now his touch, featherlight brushes of fingers over parts of her body that were definitely not office appropriate.


He grabbed the muscle of her thigh, her skirt riding up until she could see the soft indents of his fingers in her skin, and guided one leg and then the other over his until she was straddling his lap. Maggie’s knees sank into the soft couch, and as he looked up at her, he brought his lips to her ear. “Is this okay?” he asked, checking in as they pushed the boundary they had set earlier. In response, she held his face in her hands, bringing her mouth to his. There was no urgency in their kiss, only soft, long strokes of her tongue against his. His fingers traced her spine as the kiss built.


“I am beginning to see the appeal of the fainting couch,” he moaned into her neck as he trailed kisses down toward her breasts. She held on to the back of the couch, arching her back to give him more access while his hands continued to roam her body, grasping at her hips to keep her seated on his lap. Then his hand moved over to the pocket of her skirt, and he grabbed the paper sticking out of it.


Distracted by the work he was doing at her neck, her breasts, she did not see him start to unfold Dot’s note until he stopped what he was doing to read it. She squealed and managed to squeak, “That’s not your business!” But he already had the note open with a cocky grin on his face. She still tried to grab it, but Arthur deftly hooked his arm around her waist and laid her down on the couch until he was on top of her.


“Dot seems to think you’ve done well for yourself,” he said, practically preening.


“She’s in her nineties, not dead.”


“So you do think I’m attractive,” he said, as if he’d made some shocking discovery.


She rolled her eyes. “You know you are.”


“Maybe. But I like to hear you say it.”


She reached up and cupped his cheek. He leaned into the touch, a soft and intimate gesture that made Maggie’s chest constrict. “Your good looks have been driving me to distraction since the day the pall fell,” she admitted. “I couldn’t get any work done because I kept staring at your stupid hair and your shoulders and your forearms and—”


He interrupted her rambling by dipping his head down and kissing her, softer still.


“Do you remember my welcome reception?” Arthur asked when he came up for air.


Maggie tilted her head in confusion. “Sure. I was there.”


“You were.” He dragged his thumb along her bottom lip, slightly swollen from when he’d sucked it into his mouth just moments ago. “You were wearing this same skirt.” His fingers grazed the hem. “And when you came up to me, you had this lovely smile on your face. That was the first time I noticed your lips. The first time I wondered what it would be like to kiss you.”


“That was before—”


“Well before Beltane, Maggie.” His fingers at the hem of her skirt rose higher, gripping the curve of her ass. His touch couldn’t distract her from what he was saying, though. He remembered what she was wearing that day? Gods above, she didn’t know how to feel. “You didn’t get flustered when you talked to me. You didn’t ask about my research.” As he spoke, he hiked her leg farther over his hip. “In fact, you barely said ‘Hello, welcome,’ before you went back to talking to Dahlia.”


“You liked me because I was rude?”


He smirked. “Maybe. A little.” His hips dipped into hers, just enough that it felt scandalous. “Then I went to your community lecture.”


She shot up, nearly colliding with his head, but he dodged out of the way. “You did?” She was incredulous. “The one I gave in October?”


He nodded, easing her back onto the couch. “That’s when I fell in love with how you think.” Maggie tried not to think about that word, not here in their office, not with him between her legs. She swallowed as he went on. “I went to the library and read some of your research.”


“Stop, this might be the hottest thing anyone has ever said to me,” she said with a soft laugh. “You’d better not be lying just to get me to fuck you in this office.”


He leaned down, and she thought he was going to kiss her, but instead he began reciting something in her ear. “Hand in hand, walking through eastern fields of gilded yarrow—” he whispered, nuzzling her neck as he said it.


“Are you for real?” He ignored her. That was her translation, the one she had been working on for years.


“The near autumn sun anoints your brow in a shining crown,” he went on, each word perfectly recited. “Furrowed there, in deep grooves like wounds, are tomorrow’s sorrows. Bury my body, love.” The next words were swallowed as he kissed her neck, her ear. Maggie felt like she was short-circuiting from this revelation, from the way he was lavishing her skin with his mouth.


“You read my translation of Branagh’s Aubade?” she asked.


“What you’ve published of it, yes. It’s beautiful.”


Maggie wrapped her arms around his neck and pulled him down to her, kissing him again, her fingers trailing along the hard line of his belt. This time, she pulled his lip into her mouth, biting it lightly, and he sank farther into her, their clothing nothing but frustrating friction between them. “I went to your community lecture, too,” Maggie admitted.


He didn’t stop kissing her as he asked, “And what did you think?”


“I was spectacularly annoyed that you were as brilliant as advertised.” He laughed dryly. “It’s not fair how accomplished you are.” He nipped her ear, and she squirmed beneath him. “In all facets of life,” she added, gasping.


“There is only one thing I care about being good at right now,” he said as he played with the stretchy waistband of her skirt.


Even as her hips tilted up toward him, she said, “Don’t forget the rules.”


He returned to safe territory, tracing circles over her clothing. “Are you sure you want me to remember the rules, Maggie?” he asked in his wicked voice, the one that could persuade her to do almost anything if he just growled her name.


She squirmed beneath him, hating the rules she’d invented. The door is locked, she reasoned. Campus might as well be empty. There aren’t even any summer classes running right now.


She opened her mouth to give in, when the timer they had set earlier went off. Arthur smiled, as if he’d known all along they were coming close to the time, and gave one last slow stroke of her spine, one last lingering kiss, before they stood to return to the botany lab.

沙发午休：一小时空白——两人各捧小说毯子盖腿；他的手在她裙面画圈越画越高——她合书锁门。

facts.fact: 餐巾曝光：Dot 似乎认为你觅得好亲——practically preening；她辩她 90 岁不是死了。
九个月档案：迎新酒会同一条裙子——第一次注意到你的嘴唇；她不慌不忙没问研究——喜欢我因为无礼？Maybe. A little.。

facts.fact: 十月讲座：爱上你思考的方式；会后去图书馆读她已发表的研究——她笑骂最性感的话。
facts.anchor: That’s when I fell in love with how you think.

facts.fact: 当众背诵：Hand in hand, walking through eastern fields of gilded yarrow——她的译文从他口中放出；Bury my body, love 被吻吞掉后半句。
她也交底：我也去了你的讲座——spectacularly annoyed that you were as brilliant as advertised。
